   built into kanon as +bool): its terms are boolean literals, variables and
   the nodes of the module, which Kanon places in the types below. Only its Lean model matters here, in lean/: the OCaml types
   below are those that a module of terms could define, but the example is not
   compiled as OCaml. *)

[@@@lean_root "BoolExample"]

type var [@ocaml "string"] [@lean "Int"] [@noeq]

type kind [@ocaml "t_kind"] [@noeq] =
  | Var of var
  | Unop of unop * t [@operators]
  | Binop of binop * t * t [@operators]
  | Triop of triop * t * t * t [@operators]
  | Nop of nop * t list [@operators]

type unop
type binop
type triop
type nop = Distinct
type ty

  | Var of var
  | Unop of unop * t [@operators]
  | Binop of binop * t * t [@operators]

type binop
type ty

node Int of int [@literal int]
node Not : TBool -> TBool
node And : TBool -> TBool -> TBool [@comm] [@idem] [@unit true]
    [@zero false]
node Plus : TInt -> TInt -> TInt [@comm]
node Eq : a -> b -> TBool when a = b [@comm]
node TBool
node TInt

infix "&&" = And, and_
infix "+" = Plus, plus
infix "==" = Eq, eq
prefix "not" = Not, not_

constant "true" (v) = v_true
constant "false" (v) = v_false

prim equal : t -> t -> bool
prim int : int -> t
prim v_true : t
prim v_false : t

fn of_bool (b : bool) : t = if b then v_true else v_false

rule plus : Plus (v1, v2) =
  | lits: #x + #y -> int (x + y)
  | zero: x + 0 -> x

rule not_ : Not v =
  | lit: true -> v_false
  | not_not: not x -> x

rule and_ : And (v1, v2) =
  | not_: x && not y when equal x y -> v_false

rule eq : Eq (v1, v2) =
  | same: x == x -> v_true
  | lits: #x == #y -> of_bool (x = y)

use "rules"

type var [@ocaml "string"] [@lean "String"] [@noeq]

type kind [@ocaml "t_kind"] [@noeq] =
  | Var of var
  | Unop of unop * t [@operators]
  | Binop of binop * t * t [@operators]

type binop
type ty

node Int of int [@literal int]
node Not : TBool -> TBool [@invol]
node And : TBool -> TBool -> TBool [@comm] [@idem] [@unit true] [@zero false]
node Plus : TInt -> TInt -> TInt [@comm]
node Eq : a -> b -> TBool when a = b [@comm]
node TBool
node TInt

(* Primitives: implemented by hand, in OCaml (in the module P) and in Lean. *)
prim equal : t -> t -> bool
prim int : int -> t
prim v_true : t
prim v_false : t

(* Helpers *)
fn of_bool (b : bool) : t = if b then v_true else v_false

(* Rule functions: the laws of their spec come first, then these rules. *)

rule not_ : Not v =
  | true_: true -> v_false
  | false_: false -> v_true

rule and_ : And (v1, v2) =
  | not_: x && not x -> v_false

rule plus : Plus (v1, v2) =
  | lits: #x + #y -> int (x + y)
  | zero: x + 0 -> x
  | assoc: (x + #a) + #b -> x + int (a + b)

rule eq : Eq (v1, v2) =
  | same: x == x -> v_true
  | lits: #x == #y -> of_bool (x = y)
  | true_: true == x -> x
  | neg: #x == y when x < 0 && is_nat y -> v_false

(* Whether a term is surely a natural number. *)
fn is_nat (v : t) : bool =
  match v with
  | Int n -> n >= 0
  | l + r -> is_nat l && is_nat r
  | _ -> false

/-- Every rule function refines its spec, for any amount of fuel. -/
  theorem opsN_sound (orc : Oracle) (h : orc.Compat) :
  ∀ n, (opsN orc n).Sound
  | 0 =>
    { orc := h,
      not_ := fun v => Refinement.refl,
      and_ := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl,
      plus := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl,
      eq := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl }
  | n + 1 =>
    have hO := opsN_sound orc h n
    { orc := hO.orc,
      not_ := not_.step_sound _ hO,
      and_ := and_.step_sound _ hO,
      plus := plus.step_sound _ hO,
      eq := eq.step_sound _ hO }

/-- Every rule function refines its spec, for any amount of fuel. -/
  theorem opsN_sound (orc : Oracle) (h : orc.Compat) :
  ∀ n, (opsN orc n).Sound
  | 0 =>
    { orc := h,
      b_and := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl,
      b_or := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl,
      b_not := fun sv => Refinement.refl,
      b_ite := fun guard if_ else_ => Refinement.refl,
      sem_eq := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl,
      sem_eq_untyped := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl,
      b_distinct := fun l => Refinement.refl,
      plus := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl,
      int_lt := fun v1 v2 => Refinement.refl }
  | n + 1 =>
    have hO := opsN_sound orc h n
    { orc := hO.orc,
      b_and := b_and.step_sound _ hO,
      b_or := b_or.step_sound _ hO,
      b_not := b_not.step_sound _ hO,
      b_ite := b_ite.step_sound _ hO,
      sem_eq := sem_eq.step_sound _ hO,
      sem_eq_untyped := sem_eq_untyped.step_sound _ hO,
      b_distinct := b_distinct.step_sound _ hO,
      plus := plus.step_sound _ hO,
      int_lt := int_lt.step_sound _ hO }
